scope: Warrior first skill snap top-down slash: fixed path, 187.5ms traversal, compact surrounding impact, rapid decay within one second

sourcePolicy.jitterDiagnosis: Previous independently redrawn frames wobbled, while the stabilized revision reused one path but spread the descent over fifteen frames and therefore read as a falling object.
sourcePolicy.userTemporalOverride: The visible cut must cross the path only during F06-F08, hit hard on F08-F09, show compact surrounding effects, and decay before F16 without an ornate finisher.

commonPrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D combat VFX overlay sprite sheet for AlarmQuest. Create exactly 16 chronological animation frames in a strict 4-column by 4-row, row-major sprite sheet. Every cell is an independent wide 361:160 combat viewport; final sheet 1444:640; Detailed hand-painted high-resolution 2D rendering; transparent RGBA; fixed camera, fixed scale, clean antialiased alpha, image-rendering auto, no pixel art. This is the warrior's first and weakest skill, but it must feel authored and physically sharp. Motion grammar: LOCKED_SPLINE_SNAP_CUT_IMPACT. Define one immutable top-to-bottom cubic Bézier cut axis for the whole sheet: P0=(38%,7%), P1=(39%,28%), P2=(51%,57%), P3=(61%,79%). Never redraw, rotate, bend, scale, or horizontally shift this axis. Keep the same tangent, contact point, 2-3 px ivory razor core, 8-12 px translucent gunmetal pressure ribbon, and one broken desaturated-blue secondary wake whenever they are visible. The actual traversal lasts only three frames: F06-F08, at most 187.5ms. Do not gradually reveal or move the slash through F02-F15. Frame choreography: F01 almost fully clear. F02-F05 show only a tiny compressed pressure notch and two faint short air creases near P0, with no continuous slash line and no downward travel. F06 is a tight coiled preflash confined to the upper 18% of the axis. F07 is the decisive motion frame: the razor-pressure head has already crossed about 70% of the full path, with a long tapered motion smear locked to the same axis; this must read as instantaneous acceleration, not falling. F08 is hard contact at P3: show the complete connected top-to-bottom cut for one frame, terminating in a compact hooked steel wedge against one short resistance facet. F09 is the unique energy maximum immediately after contact: keep the contact wedge connected to the cut and add surrounding local effects—two asymmetric short pressure crescents peeling left and right from the lower half, six to eight small triangular steel chips, two or three muted amber sparks, and one narrow compressed-gust halo broken into segments. These surrounding effects may briefly spread across 55-70% of the cell width and 60-85% of its height, but remain low-alpha and subordinate to the blade core. They must not form a circle, flower, X, giant explosion, or second attack. F10-F12 send the same pressure fragments and chips slightly outward along the cut tangent while their total energy falls rapidly: F10 at most 70% of F09, F11 at most 48%, F12 at most 28%. F13-F15 retain only a few isolated low-alpha fragments at 16%, 9%, and 4% energy. F16 is almost fully transparent. The visible rhythm must read: stillness, coil, instantaneous top-down cut, one crisp 'TAK' impact, compact surrounding release, disappearance. Use one physical material language: cold gunmetal, desaturated blue-gray pressure, ivory razor edge, and tiny muted amber contact accents. Leave broad transparent space and keep it clearly weaker than later skills. Treat every cell as a separately clipped final viewport with no neighboring-frame residue. Render only VFX; no character, enemy, weapon body, scenery, ground, UI, text, labels, grid, borders, gutters, padding, or opaque background.

skills.name: 칼날 베기
skills.generationPrompt: Regenerate '칼날 베기' from scratch as one fast, forceful top-to-bottom blade-pressure cut. The previous stabilized version felt slow because its tip descended across fifteen frames; this version must reserve F01-F05 for nearly invisible anticipation and make the entire visible traversal happen only across F06, F07, and F08. F06 is a compressed upper preflash, F07 has already crossed roughly 70% of the fixed path with a hard tapered speed smear, and F08 slams into the fixed lower-right contact point. Reuse the exact same immutable Bézier axis, tangent, curvature, core thickness, scale, and contact position so nothing wobbles or swims. On F09, create compact but satisfying surrounding release: two unequal broken air-pressure crescents on both sides of the lower cut, six to eight small gunmetal chips, only two or three amber sparks, and a narrow segmented compression halo. Keep all release shapes physically connected to the contact and visibly subordinate to the ivory blade core. Fade them sharply during F10-F12 and leave almost nothing in F13-F16. Add richness through the coordinated razor core, steel-pressure ribbon, broken secondary wake, contact wedge, and local air tears—not through a big magical explosion. One attack only, no second hit and no ornate finishing pose. VFX only; no body, sword object, enemy, ground, scenery, UI, or lettering.
